title: Missing AutoPay Discount — 87 Accounts, One Root Cause
description: AutoPay discount not applied despite customer eligibility and no payment-method change detected. Root cause: a CGCM system sync failure during the Feb 12 maintenance window. The errors are not random — one failed sync produced all 87.
action: Review the 87 impacted accounts and Apply Fix to All — returns $870 to customers and prevents an estimated 63 support calls.

confidence.rationale: The correction is not an estimate: current minus corrected equals the exact autopay discount that failed to apply, read from the eligibility rules the sync should have honoured. Seventeen of the 87 score below 90% and can be excluded or escalated rather than assumed.

title: Duplicate Device Installments — Highest Dollar Impact
description: Device-loan installment charges appearing twice for the same IMEI in the current billing cycle. A LoanSys replication timing issue wrote each installment twice; the ledger shows both, and the customer is billed for both.
action: Bulk-correct the duplicates — the largest per-pattern dollar impact in this cycle.

confidence.rationale: A duplicate is identified by matching IMEI plus installment sequence within the cycle, not by amount similarity — so a legitimate second device on the same account is not caught by this pattern.

title: International Roaming Overcharge — Highest Confidence
description: Mexico and Canada roaming charges applied despite the plan including free roaming in those countries. The roaming feature flag was not mapped after the plan-update rollout, so entitlements the customer already has were never consulted.
action: Reverse the overcharges in bulk — 96% confidence, the highest of the six patterns.

confidence.rationale: Entitlement is a boolean on the plan record, and the usage-rating engine logs the country per session. The check is a direct comparison rather than an inference, which is why this pattern scores highest.

title: Incorrect State Tax Calculation — Stale Rate Table
description: State tax calculated using an outdated rate table: 12% applied where the updated jurisdiction rate is 7%. The tax engine never picked up the January 2026 rate changes, so the error is systematic rather than per-account.
action: Apply the corrected tax rate in bulk, and escalate the rule-version fix to Platform Admin so next cycle does not repeat it.

confidence.rationale: The rate table carries a version stamp, so the comparison is between two known versions rather than a judgment about which rate is correct. The dollar impact is small; the compliance exposure is not.

escalation.reason: Rule-version fix is a platform change, not a billing correction

title: Plan Migration Rate Mismatch — Lowest-Confidence Bulk Pattern
description: Customers migrated to a new unlimited plan are still charged old rate-card pricing. A rate-card sync delay between ORBPM and the billing system means the migration landed in one system and not the other.
action: Reprice to the correct rate card after confirming migration effective dates — at 85% this is the one bulk pattern worth checking before applying.

confidence.rationale: Effective dates are the weak link: where a migration date is ambiguous the correct rate is genuinely uncertain, so this pattern sits in the operator-review tier rather than the auto-resolve one.

title: Five Edge Cases That Fit No Pattern
description: Unique billing anomalies with no shared root cause — the residue after grouping. Five accounts, $1,068.20, and the highest dollar-per-account of the cycle. These are the ones worth an operator's actual attention.
action: Investigate individually and escalate to SME where the cause is not established.

confidence.rationale: Deliberately low. These did not group because nothing explains them yet; the score reflects that the system can say a charge is wrong without being able to say why. That is what makes them individual work.
